two_sided_statements.statement: A person should stay even-minded and not grieve over death, loss of loved ones, or changing fortunes.
A person should honor, obey and care for their parents while alive and mourn them with proper rites.
A person should feel painful emotions rather than numb them, while keeping grief from destroying their life.
A person should schedule their workday in advance and stop working at a fixed time each day.
A person should remember death is coming and do good in this life rather than worrying about the afterlife.
A person should be truthful, keep their word, and never pretend to be what they are not.
A person should demand much of themselves, aim high, and believe their abilities can grow through effort.
A person should honor and obey their parents and elder siblings and fulfil their family duties.
A person should worship the deity with wholehearted faith and devotion, meditating on it constantly.
A person should care for their own health, resources and future as they would for someone in their charge.
A person should see the same soul in all beings and love friends, strangers and enemies equally.
A person should respect parents, elders, rulers and traditional laws rather than following momentary whims.
A person should guard their mind against disturbance from outside things, including passion-stirring art and poetry.
A person should perform traditional rites and honor ancestors, gods and parents with sincere reverence.
A person should devote their life to seeking liberation by realizing their identity with ultimate reality, never returning to worldly life.
A person should work or practice steadily within set routines, avoiding excess.
A person should not grieve over loss, death or hardship, but bear it calmly.
A person should keep their own death in mind and use that to focus on doing good in this life.
A person should act cautiously, keep resources in reserve, and avoid needless risks.
A person should fix their mind on the deity within and serve it through their work rather than through ritual prayers alone.
A person should fix their mind on the deity and, if unable, serve it through work done without seeking its fruits.
A person should worship the deity alone with wholehearted faith, devoting every action and prayer to it.
A person should detach from sensual pleasures, family ties and the pursuit of wealth to free themselves from craving.
A person should investigate the truth for themselves rather than blindly accept others' beliefs, while staying open to being wrong.
A person should see themselves as ordinary and equal to others rather than special.
A person should withdraw from sense pleasures and meditate to realize the Self as one with ultimate reality.
A person should rely on the material world and their own powers instead of faith and prayer to the divine.
